text:
kevin: Hey team — customer reported a sudden spike in p99 for generation endpoints starting ~10:10 UTC, lasting ~20–30m. They sent req_id=abc123 and said responses were stuck in queueing for ~6s. Posting logs here: https://redwood.internal/logs/abc123 (gzipped). Can eng-infra or runtime take a look? :exclamation:

jasmin: Thanks — I can take the initial triage. Any service/node IDs? Which model/route?

kevin: route=api.v1.generate, model=redwood-large-v1, tenant=acme-corp, example request size ~600 tokens. Node ids in log: worker-7c9f, worker-3a2b.

ops-bot: ALERT: ingress-queue-depth > 500 for cluster-east-1 for 10m. avg_admit_latency=1800ms, p99_admit_latency=6200ms.

mira: Noted. I see a concurrent spike in prefix cache ops and memory allocations on worker-7c9f around the same time. Possible KV-cache GC or buffer-starvation causing backpressure.

sam: Can we get a quick repro here? Is this sustained or a burst? If burst, admission control may be thrashing.

kevin: Customer says it was a burst from a batch job — sustained ~200 rps for 2m then dropped. They attached a replay with header X-Req-ID: abc123.

jasmin: Replaying on staging now with same token length. Initial run shows requests queuing behind long-lived attention ops on a few workers — concurrency_limit=16 configured. When overload hits, helpers starve.

mira: Two actionable mitigations: 1) temporarily lower per-worker concurrency to 8 to avoid head-of-line blocking, 2) enable fast-fail for oversized requests so they don't pile into the admit queue. I can push config change if we agree.

sam: +1. Also let's bump temporary pool size by +2 workers in cluster-east-1 to soak the burst while we investigate root cause. Rolling restart might be required for a config-driven change.

jasmin: Paste of commands I ran locally to test admission behaviour (staging):
```
# run a small replay against staging ingress
ab -n 1000 -c 50 -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST" 
  -p payload.json https://staging-api.redwood/v1/generate
# observe /metrics
curl https://staging-api.redwood/metrics | grep admit_queue_depth
```

kevin: Customer-facing note: I've told them we're investigating and will apply a temporary mitigation within 15 minutes.

ops-bot: RUNBOOK SUGGESTION: For short congestion bursts, set admit_threshold_ms -> 1200ms and enable admit_fail_fast=true for tenant-affecting routes.

mira: I'm going to apply admit_threshold_ms=1200 and concurrency_limit=8 on cluster-east-1 ingress for the next 30m. Rolling update, no downtime expected. Will watch metrics.

sam: Also enable a temporary autoscale bump: increase desired replicas from 12 -> 14 for the serving pool. I can run kubectl, but want @oncall sign-off.

jasmin: I ran a quick replay after lowering concurrency and enabling fast-fail — p99 dropped from ~6.2s to ~1.1s in staging. Admit queue depth also fell from 520 -> 70.

kevin: Great — telling the customer we applied mitigations. Will monitor and report.

mira: Applied changes in prod (cluster-east-1):
```
# patch admit config
kubectl patch cm ingress-config -n redwood --patch '{"data":{"admit_threshold_ms":"1200","concurrency_limit":"8","admit_fail_fast":"true"}}'
# scale pool
kubectl scale deployment/serve-pool -n redwood --replicas=14
```
Observing now. Metrics look promising.

sam: Can we capture flamegraphs for worker-7c9f and worker-3a2b during the next spike? I suspect a memory-copy hot path that stalls other goroutines.

jasmin: Yes — I added a short profiler run to the postmortem logs. If we reproduce, I'll upload traces.

support-bot: NOTE: Notifying customer that a mitigation was applied and asking for impact confirmation.

kevin: Customer replied: "Latency improved, problem seems mitigated for now. We'll continue to monitor. Please let us know root cause."

mira: Next steps: 1) collect heap/CPU profiles for the two workers, 2) audit recent kernel/driver updates that might affect GPU memory behavior, 3) add more conservative default concurrency for large-token routes. I'll open an RFC for default change.

sam: +1, I'll coordinate the flamegraph capture and correlate with KV cache metrics. If we find a bug in buffer allocation we should hotfix in runtime and schedule a canary rollout.

jasmin: Adding repro artifacts to the incident thread: small replay script, payload.json, and staging metrics snapshots.

kevin: Thanks all. I'll keep customer updated and mark as 'mitigated' until we have root cause. :white_check_mark:
